chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property directly indicates the subject matter of a creative work or event, which aligns with the definition of 'has subject' for these instances.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage

Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim

Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: size
candidates.comment: The standardized dimensions or measurement of a product or creative work. Also called dimensions, measurement, product size, item size. Examples: `T-Shirt` size `"XL"`, `Book` size `SizeSpecification: 6x9 inches`, `Shoe` size `QuantitativeValue: 10 US`. Distinct from `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, which are specific dimensions.

candidates.label: checkinTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the earliest time for check-in. Also called "arrival time", "earliest check-in", "check-in starts". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkinTime '15:00'", "Flight reservation checkinTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00'". Distinct from checkoutTime, which specifies the latest time for departure.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

candidates.label: publishedBy

Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: volumeNumber
candidates.comment: A volume number relation between a publication volume and its identifying number or text within a multi-part work. Also called publication volume, series volume, book volume. Examples: "PublicationVolume volumeNumber '2'", "PublicationVolume volumeNumber 'iii'", "Journal issue volumeNumber '10'".

candidates.label: sdDatePublished
candidates.comment: The date when the structured data associated with a creative work was generated or published. Also called structured data publication date, metadata publish date, data generation date. Examples: `Article JSON-LD` sdDatePublished `2023-10-26`, `Recipe Structured Data` sdDatePublished `2023-09-15`, `Event Markup` sdDatePublished `2023-08-01`. Distinct from `datePublished`, which is the publication date of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: issn
candidates.comment: A serial publication identification relation between a blog, creative work series, dataset, or website and its International Standard Serial Number. Also called serial identifier, ISSN number, publication code. Examples: A journal has an issn of '1234-5678'. A magazine series has an issn of '9876-5432'. An online blog has an issn of '2345-6789'. Distinct from isbn, which is for books.

chosen_property.label: criticizedBy
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the entity that expressed disapproval or negative judgment towards an event or work.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links an 'Event' to a 'Person' who criticized it. 'negativeNotes' is for the negative aspects of an item, not the critic.

candidates.label: negativeNotes
candidates.comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

candidates.label: associatedReview
candidates.comment: A review related to another review. Also called: linked review, related assessment. Examples: "Review 'Product Review A' associatedReview 'Product Review B'", "Review 'Movie Review' associatedReview 'Critic Review'."

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: reviews
candidates.comment: A collection of critical assessments or evaluations pertaining to an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item reviews, evaluations, critiques, assessments. Examples: `Product: Laptop` reviews `[Review 1, Review 2, ...]`, `Movie: Dune` reviews `[Critic Review, User Review]`, `Restaurant: Pizzeria` reviews `[Google Reviews, Yelp Reviews]`. Distinct from `review`, which typically refers to a single review.

candidates.label: reviewRating
candidates.comment: The specific rating provided within a review. Also called rating in review, review's score, individual rating. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewRating `5 stars`, `Film Critic Review` reviewRating `8/10`, `Restaurant Review` reviewRating `3 out of 5`. Distinct from `aggregateRating`, which is the overall rating of the review *as a creative work*, not the rating *given by* the review.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: inverseOf
candidates.comment: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.

candidates.label: nonEqual
candidates.comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: domainIncludes
candidates.comment: A domain inclusion relation between a property and a class, indicating that the property is expected to be used on instances of that class. Also called "applies to type", "valid for class", "used with". Examples: "Property 'name' domainIncludes 'Thing'", "Property 'author' domainIncludes 'CreativeWork'", "Property 'price' domainIncludes 'Offer'".

candidates.label: usageInfo
candidates.comment: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: shippingOrigin
candidates.comment: The geographical region or location from which a shipment originates. Also called shipment source, origin of delivery, dispatch location. Examples: `Offer Shipping Details` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: California`, `Shipping Conditions` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: Warehouse A`, `International Shipment` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: China`. Distinct from `shippingDestination`, which is where the shipment goes.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: follows

candidates.label: tracks

candidates.label: track

candidates.label: observationPeriod

Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". candidates.label: deliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A logistical approach relation between an order, receive, send, or track action and the method used for delivery. Also called: shipping method, delivery mode, transport method. Examples: "Online Purchase" delivery method "Standard Shipping", "Document Send" delivery method "Email", "Package Tracking" delivery method "Courier Service".

candidates.label: trackingNumber
candidates.comment: A tracking number relation between a parcel delivery and its unique identifier provided by the shipper. Also called shipment ID, parcel ID, delivery tracking code. candidates.label: recordingOf

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: pattern
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the visual or design pattern of a creative work or product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A dress has a pattern of 'polka dot'. A fabric has a pattern of 'striped'. A flag has a pattern of 'Canadian flag'.

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: countryOfAssembly
candidates.comment: A manufacturing location relation between a product and the country where it was assembled. Also called: assembled in, manufacturing country, assembly location. Examples: "Smartphone" country of assembly "China", "Car" country of assembly "Mexico", "Laptop" country of assembly "Vietnam". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: recipeIngredient
candidates.comment: A recipe ingredient relation between a recipe and the components, often with quantities, required for its preparation. Also called ingredients for, recipe components, required items. Examples: "A cake recipe includes recipe ingredients '2 cups flour'.", "A salad recipe lists recipe ingredients 'lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber'.", "A stew recipe requires recipe ingredients 'beef, potatoes, carrots'."
